host: host-a for the round counts, host-c for the sizes
question: Three: would a non-elliptic-curve scheme make the matched field cheaper, what throughput does the matched field leave cross-region, and what does post-quantum cost.

non_elliptic_curve.answer: no, and the repository already measured why
non_elliptic_curve.reasoning: The matched field's cost is set by the field *size*, and 128-bit security forces a scalar field of about 256 bits for any discrete-log group --- elliptic curve or multiplicative. So no discrete-log scheme shrinks the MPC field. What the group choice does change is the speed of the proofs themselves, and there the curve wins by a lot.
non_elliptic_curve.the_one_direction_that_could: Lattice commitments. Their security comes from dimension rather than modulus size, so a homomorphic commitment can live over a 32- or 64-bit modulus and the MPC field could shrink with it. What stops it is not the size but the shape: lattice sigma protocols need rejection sampling, so the response is not a clean linear function of the witness, and threshold_sigma's whole method --- each node computes its own piece of the response and they Lagrange-combine --- does not survive that.

cross_region_throughput.superseded: The first version of this section extrapolated from a batching table taken at 15 ms in a different configuration, assuming the matched field's round penalty stays at the 2.02x it shows at Q=1. It does not. Measured at 120 ms one way, the penalty grows with the batch --- 2.02x at Q=1, 3.87x at Q=8, 5.07x at Q=32 --- and rounds grow at 6.29 a quote in the default field against 38.23 in the matched one, where the extrapolation used 3.48 and 7.02. The old figure of 0.38 quotes a second was ten times too generous.
cross_region_throughput.note: host-a carried a load average near 60 during this run, so the wall clock is an inflated upper bound. Rounds and bytes do not depend on load, and the round-trip floor computed from them does not either --- both say the same thing. The Q=1 default-field figure of 26.7 s also matches placement_intercontinental.json's 26.1 s, so the instrument agrees with itself.
cross_region_throughput.finding: Batching pays in the default field and does not in the matched one. Default: Q=1 to Q=32 takes 26.7 s a quote to 3.3 s, eight times better, while the age goes 27 s to 107 s, four times worse --- a good trade against staleness.json, where 96 s is 1.34 to 1.75 times the within-block floor. Matched: 57.5 s to 27.8 s a quote, twice better, while the age goes 57 s to 889 s, fifteen times worse. A quote fifteen minutes old is not a quote.
cross_region_throughput.conclusion: Cross-region, the matched field is usable only un-batched, at 57 s and 0.017 quotes a second. Batching it trades staleness for throughput at about seven to one. And 8,932 MB a job is 1,276 MB a node, which a gigabit link spends ten seconds a job moving. The default field with the input check is what runs cross-region: 0.300 quotes a second at Q=32 with a 107-second quote, and the binding costs one round.

post_quantum.what_is_already_post_quantum: The confidential computation itself. Shamir secret sharing with an honest majority is information-theoretically secure --- there is no assumption for a quantum computer to break, so the MPC layer needs nothing.
post_quantum.the_favourable_half: Pedersen commitments are *perfectly* hiding and only computationally binding. A quantum adversary can open a commitment to a value it does not hold; it can never learn the value. So what quantum takes away is the ability to prove, never the ability to hide.
what_breaks: Ed25519 signatures on shares and slot receipts
the sigma protocols and the quote proof
adaptor signatures in the cross-ledger settlement
post_quantum.the_cost_is_size_not_speed: ML-DSA signs and verifies at speeds comparable to Ed25519 in optimised implementations. What it costs here is bytes, and the maker update path is where they land.
post_quantum.no_pq_implementation_was_benchmarked: dilithium-py gives the standard sizes, which is what the byte counts here use, but it is pure Python and its timings would not represent an optimised implementation. No timing is claimed.
post_quantum.and_this_meets_the_first_question: Post-quantum homomorphic commitments are lattice commitments, which is the same direction that could shrink the matched field --- and the same rejection sampling blocks both. The two questions have one answer.

single_prover.note: policy_audit.py and state_audit.py do not import threshold_sigma --- a maker proving about its own policy needs no help

threshold_assembled.note: and this is the system's headline claim

three_obstacles.name: size
three_obstacles.detail: 4,960 bytes a step measured for a sigma proof here; lattice equivalents are kilobytes to tens of kilobytes, from the literature. Bandwidth, and the design does not change.

three_obstacles.name: rejection sampling
three_obstacles.detail: the abort test is on the combined response rather than on any share, so the nodes would have to reconstruct it to decide, and a rejection then comes after the leak it exists to prevent. Two to seven expected retries, each needing fresh randomness across all nodes: a one-shot assembly becomes an interactive protocol.

three_obstacles.name: shortness against Shamir
three_obstacles.detail: lattice soundness needs a short witness; Shamir shares are uniform in Z_q and Lagrange coefficients are arbitrary elements of it, and combine_responses multiplies the two and reduces. Shortness does not survive. Not a tunable parameter --- a mismatch between how Shamir reconstructs and what lattice soundness requires.

ways_out.replicated_secret_sharing: reconstruction is a plain sum with {0,1} coefficients so shortness survives; at n=7 T=2 that is C(7,2)=21 shares with C(6,2)=15 per party, so fifteen times the per-party storage, and it does not scale past small n
ways_out.threshold_lattice_signatures: active research; known constructions are heavier than the plain scheme and need more rounds

quantum_network.question: Does QKD or a quantum network change any of this?
quantum_network.the_one_place_it_helps: The MPC is information-theoretically secure but the traffic between the nodes runs over TLS, so an eavesdropper who records every link today and breaks TLS later holds every share. The computation is unconditional and the pipe carrying it is not. Seven fixed long-lived endpoints in one metropolitan area --- which section 0 already recommends for latency --- is also the shape and range QKD can serve.

but_not_as_a_one_time_pad.note: Traffic figures are measured; the QKD key rate is a literature range for metro distances and is not measured here.
but_not_as_a_one_time_pad.conclusion: One to two orders of magnitude short even on the cheapest row. A deployment would rekey a symmetric cipher instead, and symmetric ciphers are already quantum-safe --- Grover halves the effective key strength and AES-256 absorbs it. So the real gain is narrower than it sounds: not having to trust the key-exchange assumption. Against store-now-decrypt-later that is still a genuine defence.

where_it_cannot_help.commitments: Unconditionally secure bit commitment is impossible even with quantum mechanics (Mayers; Lo-Chau, 1997). This is a no-go theorem rather than an engineering limit, so the lattice work is not avoidable by building a quantum network instead.
where_it_cannot_help.the_quote_proof: A proof has to convince someone who was not on the link --- an auditor, a supervisor, a counterparty checking years later. QKD secures a channel between two parties who are both present.
where_it_cannot_help.signatures: Quantum digital signature schemes exist but need quantum memory or repeated distribution and their transferability is limited, so they do not give 'anyone can verify this afterwards'. ML-DSA or its kind is still needed.
where_it_cannot_help.quantum_secret_sharing: The shares here are classical values, so the benefit collapses into the channel row above.
where_it_cannot_help.anonymous_transmission: Would hide which participant sent a request --- the transport layer's job, approximated today by batching and shuffling on a fixed schedule. Theoretically stronger, practically remote.

quantum_network.the_line: A quantum network makes the pipe unconditional, not the proof. And the proof side has an impossibility result on it, so the lattice work stays on the list either way.
